label: early copy steps (2nd/3rd output) of long sequences, token-gated (n, v, r, ...)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at the first two copy steps after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, about 83% of mass, and recall_idx 2, about 17%), and only in long sequences (L=9 holds 85% of mass, L=8 14%, nothing for L<=6). Equivalently, to_go is 6-7. Silent on the original phase, the <DEL> step, later copy steps and short sequences. Within that window, the input token sets magnitude: at recall_idx 1 the input is orig(0), and the strongest activations are when it is n (or v), e.g. n ... <DEL> [n:1.0]. Other letters such as r, i, u, j, l, m give weaker firing, and many tokens (t, f, q, o, z) rarely fire. The second-copy-step activation is usually much weaker than the first. Position alone gives recall 0.96 but precision 0.25, and the token set raises precision to about 0.48. The token preference is graded, not a clean set, so precision stays incomplete.
